math_check.verdict: Correct and consistently rounded. 'about sixty' (59.99), 'about eighty' (79.99), 'about eighty-six' (86.47), 'about six' (6.48); on screen 86 - 80 = 6 exactly, so a viewer subtracting sees no mismatch. 'Pays about eighty dollars' for $79.99 is consistent (about in voice, ~ on screen). Caveats: the $86 uses CPI-U all items NSA, not wages or a games price index; the $79.99 is the Standard edition (Ultimate is $99.99, not mentioned in the video); GTA 5 $59.99 rests on one outlet (GG Recon) plus common knowledge; GTA 6 price rests on GameLuster, not Rockstar.

claim_honesty: The number claim is honest as written ('about', 'today's money'). Two softness issues: (1) the cashier's 'bargain' is supported only as 'a bit cheaper than GTA 5 after inflation'; a $6 gap does not make $80 a bargain, so the hook oversells and the payoff under-delivers; (2) the video never says 'inflation' or 'prices, not paychecks', so 'cheaper' can be heard as 'easier to afford'. The description carries the caveat; the video should carry one short line.
post_timing: Safe for US viewers if posted 7 PM ET Nov 18 (release Nov 19 per the research file). Going stale: 7 PM ET Nov 18 is already Nov 19 morning in Manila/Asia and after midnight in Europe, so 'Tomorrow' is wrong there and for any viewer after release. No evergreen fallback in the video.
surprise_and_split: The real-terms reveal is a genuine, checkable 'huh', but moderate: many gamers have seen the inflation argument and $6 is a small gap, so 'wait, what?' is about a 6. It does split opinion in the A/B (people hate $80, others defend inflation), though 'Worth it or too much' asks about value while the video shows only price math.
